cls: Antineoplastic - anti-programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) monoclonal antibody
pharm: Humanized IgG4 anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody with engineered Fc region to minimize Fc-gamma receptor binding; blocks PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitory signaling to restore T-cell antitumor activity; used in esophageal and gastric/GEJ cancers
quick: Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 4 months after the last dose
No standard adjustment defined; monitor for immune-mediated nephritis
No standard adjustment defined; monitor for immune-mediated hepatitis
No specific interaction; limit due to additive liver effects
Immune-mediated toxicities (lung, bowel, liver, endocrine, kidney, skin), infusion reactions, LFTs, TFTs
summary: Tislelizumab (Tevimbra) is an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody with an engineered Fc region designed to reduce Fc-gamma receptor binding and macrophage-mediated T-cell clearance. By blocking the PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitory checkpoint it restores T-cell activity against tumor cells. It is indicated as a single agent for adults with unresectable or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after prior systemic chemotherapy not including a PD-(L)1 inhibitor, and in combination regimens for advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. The dose is 200 mg by intravenous infusion every 3 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The dominant risks are severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions (pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies, nephritis, dermatitis, and others) plus infusion-related reactions and embryo-fetal toxicity. There are no dose reductions; management is by withholding or permanently discontinuing plus corticosteroids.
indications: Treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after prior systemic chemotherapy that did not include a PD-(L)1 inhibitor, as a single agent
Treatment of adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, in combination with chemotherapy (including HER2-directed combinations per labeling)

dosage.c: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma or gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma
dosage.d: 200 mg by IV infusion once every 3 weeks
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; give combination chemotherapy partners per their schedules

dosage.d: No dose reduction; withhold for moderate (grade 2) events and resume only on full resolution to grade 0-1 with steroids tapered; permanently discontinue for severe, recurrent, or life-threatening (grade 3-4) events per labeling tables
dosage.n: Give systemic corticosteroids (e.g., prednisone 1-2 mg/kg/day) and taper over at least 1 month; add other immunosuppressants if no improvement

dosage.d: Slow or interrupt for grade 1-2 reactions; permanently discontinue for grade 3-4 reactions
dosage.n: Consider premedication for subsequent infusions after a mild reaction

admin: Give 200 mg as an intravenous infusion over 60 minutes for the first infusion; subsequent infusions may be given over 30 minutes if well tolerated
Do not give as IV push or bolus; use a sterile, preservative-free dilution with the recommended line filter
Inspect solution before use; do not use if particulate matter or discoloration is present
Monitor during and after infusion for infusion-related reactions; have emergency treatment available
Withhold or discontinue for immune-mediated adverse reactions per grade; do not attempt dose reduction
moa: Tislelizumab is a humanized immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody against programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1). PD-1 on T cells normally binds PD-L1/PD-L2 on tumor and stromal cells, delivering an inhibitory signal that suppresses T-cell proliferation and cytotoxic function. Tislelizumab blocks this interaction, releasing the brake on T cells and restoring antitumor immune responses. Its Fc region is specifically engineered to minimize binding to Fc-gamma receptors on macrophages, which is intended to reduce antibody-dependent phagocytosis of PD-1-positive T cells seen with some other IgG4 antibodies.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to tislelizumab or any excipient
relative: Active autoimmune disease requiring systemic immunosuppression
Prior severe immune-mediated reaction to a PD-(L)1 inhibitor
Solid organ transplant recipient (risk of rejection)
monitor: Thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal function for endocrinopathies
Creatinine for nephritis and skin for dermatitis

preg: Based on its mechanism, tislelizumab can cause fetal harm including increased risk of miscarriage, stillbirth, and neonatal death by disrupting maternal immune tolerance. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 4 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of tislelizumab in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 4 months after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is defined for renal impairment in the labeling summary. Monitor serum creatinine for immune-mediated nephritis; withhold or discontinue plus corticosteroids per grade rather than reducing the dose.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is defined for hepatic impairment in the labeling summary. Monitor liver tests for immune-mediated hepatitis; withhold or discontinue plus corticosteroids per grade rather than reducing the dose.

major: Systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants before starting - may blunt antitumor activity; avoid prophylactic use, though steroids are required to treat immune reactions
Other immune checkpoint combinations - additive immune-mediated toxicity
moderate: Live vaccines during treatment - avoid in patients receiving immunotherapy; use inactivated vaccines per guidelines
minor: No classic CYP-mediated interactions expected for a monoclonal antibody
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive hepatic effects with hepatitis risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor LFTs, creatinine, thyroid function, cortisol/ACTH as indicated, glucose, and creatine kinase; evaluate new pulmonary, bowel, skin, or neurologic symptoms promptly.

serious: Immune-mediated endocrinopathies (thyroiditis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency, type 1 diabetes)
rare: Immune-mediated neurologic events (encephalitis, Guillain-Barre syndrome, myasthenia)
emergency: New cough, chest pain, or breathlessness (pneumonitis)
Severe diarrhea, bloody stools, or severe abdominal pain (colitis)
Yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or severe fatigue (hepatitis)
Chest pain, palpitations, muscle weakness, or neurologic changes (myocarditis/neurologic events)

monitoring: Respiratory status and imaging for pneumonitis; bowel habits for colitis
Liver tests before each dose and for hepatic symptoms
Thyroid function, glucose, and pituitary/adrenal testing for endocrinopathies
Creatinine, creatine kinase, and skin exams for nephritis, myositis, and dermatitis
Infusion tolerance during and after each dose
counsel: This IV immunotherapy is given every 3 weeks; it works by activating your immune system, which can also attack healthy organs
Report new cough, chest pain, or trouble breathing right away (lung inflammation)
Report diarrhea, bloody stools, belly pain, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe tiredness promptly
Report hormone symptoms such as unusual headache, extreme fatigue, rapid heartbeat, weight change, thirst, or frequent urination
Report rash, mouth sores, muscle pain, or vision changes; use effective birth control during and for 4 months after treatment
pk: PD-1 receptor occupancy from first infusion; tumor responses assessed over weeks
Terminal half-life approximately 3-4 weeks, supporting every-3-week dosing
Steady state over several cycles; dosed every 3 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C; diluted solution per labeling time limits; do not freeze or shake; protect from light
pearls: Engineered Fc region minimizes Fc-gamma receptor binding, a design difference from some other anti-PD-1 antibodies
No dose reductions exist - toxicity management is hold versus permanently stop, plus steroids tapered over at least 1 month
Endocrinopathies (especially hypothyroidism) are common and usually managed with hormone replacement while continuing therapy
Pneumonitis, colitis, and hepatitis drive most permanent discontinuations - evaluate new symptoms before the next dose
Contraception extends 4 months after the last dose because of the long half-life and immune mechanism
missed: Tislelizumab is given as a supervised IV infusion every 3 weeks, so there is no patient-managed missed dose. If an appointment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule as soon as possible.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for tislelizumab overdose. Overdose may produce exaggerated immune-mediated or infusion reactions. Monitor closely for pulmonary, gastrointestinal, hepatic, endocrine, renal, cardiac, and dermatologic toxicity and provide supportive care including corticosteroids as indicated. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
